about.heading: Curious about data, systems, and everything in between.
paragraphs: My name is Disu Ibukunoluwa. I'm a recent First Class Computer Science graduate from Covenant University and an emerging Data Engineer. I work with SQL, Python, and data visualisation tools, with experience in data modelling, dashboard design, and root-cause analysis that supports informed decision-making.

I became interested in data because it can help us understand what happened, see what is happening now, and spot patterns that might shape what happens next. That range of possibilities is what first sparked my curiosity.

But data doesn't become useful just because it exists. It has to be collected, organised, processed, stored, and made accessible. That's what draws me to Data Engineering: building the systems that connect information to the decisions people need to make.

When I'm not writing SQL or debugging code, I enjoy public speaking, debate, reading, and bringing people together to make ideas happen. I'm also fascinated by the universe and love falling down a rabbit hole whenever something catches my interest.

Those interests influence how I approach engineering. They've taught me to ask better questions, explain ideas clearly, and think about the people relying on a system. I'm always curious, always learning, and always looking for the next problem worth solving.
If you're into data, AI, or just want to talk about the universe over coffee, I'd love to connect!

projects_intro: Practical work in data extraction, transformation, orchestration and reliability—with the decisions behind each pipeline documented.

projects.title: Bitcoin price ETL pipeline
projects.summary: A scheduled ETL pipeline that collects Bitcoin quotes from the CoinMarketCap API, cleans and transforms them using Pandas, and loads them into PostgreSQL—with a timestamped CSV fallback if the database write fails.
projects.challenge: Collect, process and store Bitcoin market data on a consistent monthly schedule for historical market analysis and reporting.
approach: Extract Bitcoin quotes in USD from the CoinMarketCap API using an authenticated request.
Normalise and clean the returned JSON using Pandas, including numeric and datetime conversion.
Load structured records into PostgreSQL, writing the processed data to a timestamped CSV when the database load fails.
Orchestrate extract_data_task, transform_data_task and load_data_task in Apache Airflow and deploy using GitHub Actions.
projects.architecture: CoinMarketCap API → Airflow extraction → Pandas transformation → PostgreSQL (fallback: timestamped CSV). DAG: crypto_dag. Cron schedule: 0 0 1 * * (first day of each month). Configured start date: June 21, 2024.

decisions.title: Separate the ETL stages
decisions.body: Explicit extraction, transformation and loading tasks keep the stages easier to reason about.

decisions.title: Preserve data during database errors
decisions.body: A CSV fallback retains the transformed output rather than discarding it after a failed PostgreSQL write.

decisions.title: Automate deployment
decisions.body: GitHub Actions deploys the Airflow workflow to an Ubuntu server.

projects.quality: A timestamped CSV fallback protects transformed records when loading to PostgreSQL fails; it does not automatically retry database ingestion.
projects.outcomes: A monthly Bitcoin market data pipeline with scheduled ingestion, PostgreSQL storage, CSV fallback, and a GitHub Actions deployment workflow.
projects.lessons: Orchestration, consistent transformation and explicit handling of downstream failures are all part of reliable data engineering.
